Head'sWelcome
CARING, DETERMINED AND REFLECTIVE
At The Malling School, we believe every young person deserves to be known, to belong and to be inspired to achieve their very best. We are proud to be a caring, ambitious and inclusive community where high expectations are matched by genuine kindness, and where every young person is supported to flourish academically, personally and socially while being empowered to shape their own future.
Sixth Form Success At Key Stage 5, students made positive progress across both academic and vocational provision, with positive value added in both areas and particularly encouraging improvement in vocational outcomes. There were also excellent academic performances, particularly in History, Psychology and Mathematics. Fifty-five per cent of Level 3 students are progressing to university, including destinations at seven Russell Group institutions – Bristol, Edinburgh, Manchester, Newcastle, Southampton, Birmingham and Exeter. Students will study courses ranging from Mathematics and Biochemistry to Law, Psychology, Geology and Cognitive Science. The school is equally proud that every vocational student has secured a positive destination, including employment, college, supported internships and specialist provision. Individual successes include: Brooke achieved an outstanding grade 7 in IB Psychology HL, alongside a grade 6 in Chemistry HL and strong results across her wider programme. Brendan achieved an impressive set of results, including grade 6s in IB Computing HL and Mathematics HL, a grade 5 in Economics HL and an A in Criminology. Yasmine achieved grade 6s in both IB English HL and Psychology HL, alongside a grade 5 in History HL. Kian combined his academic studies with an outstanding D*D* in BTEC Sport, alongside a grade 5 in IB Psychology HL. Molly achieved an excellent D*DD in BTEC Health & Social Care, while Thomas and also secured D*DD in BTEC Sport. The Malling School is incredibly proud of all its students and wishes them every success as they progress to university, further education, employment and other exciting opportunities.
GCSE Success Students at The Malling School are celebrating their GCSE and Sixth Form achievements, with results opening the door to an exciting range of university places, further education, employment and other opportunities. This year's results provide much to celebrate, with students once again demonstrating remarkable resilience, determination and commitment. Headline outcomes have remained broadly consistent, alongside encouraging areas of improvement and individual success. These results also reflect the invaluable encouragement and support of families, alongside the dedication of staff across the school who have supported students throughout their journey. GCSE Success Year 11 students achieved a positive set of GCSE and vocational results, with a particular highlight being the number securing passes in both English and Mathematics, providing them with important qualifications for their chosen post-16 pathways. Among those celebrating particularly impressive results are: Alex achieved an exceptional set of results, including grade 9s in Mathematics and Computing, 9-9 in Combined Science, grade 8s in Geography and Spanish, grade 7s in both English Language and Literature, and a Distinction* in Sport. Megan secured an excellent range of results, including 8-7 in Combined Science, grade 8s in Computing and Spanish, grade 7s in Mathematics and Geography, and a Distinction* in Sport. Olivia achieved grade 8s in Mathematics and Business, 8-7 in Combined Science, grade 7s in Geography and Spanish, alongside a Distinction* in Sport. Charley achieved an impressive set of results, including 8-7 in Combined Science, a grade 8 in Art & Design, grade 7s in English Language and Geography, and a Distinction in Music. Jake achieved strong results across the curriculum, including 8-7 in Combined Science, a grade 8 in History, and grade 7s in English Language and Computing. These successes reflect achievements across the wider year group, with students securing the qualifications needed to progress to The Malling School Sixth Form, colleges, apprenticeships and other post-16 opportunities.
A huge congratulations to all our Sixth Formers collecting their results today! We are incredibly proud of each and every one of you and all the hard work, dedication and determination you have shown along the way. Today marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter. Whatever path you choose, we wish you every success, happiness and fulfilment for the future.

Great British Summer Savings Rising prices can make life's little treats harder to afford, especially during the school holidays when costs build up for families. This Government is determined to help, and that is why last month the Chancellor announced the Great British Summer Savings scheme. From 25 June to 1 September 2026, the Government is temporarily cutting VAT from 20% to 5% on children's meals in restaurants, children and family tickets to cinemas, theatres, concerts and exhibitions, and admission to a wide range of attractions. Combined with free bus travel during August for children aged 5 to 15 in England, families and young people will be able to enjoy experiences that make summer special, including visits to the kinds of cultural and educational attractions that enrich children's lives outside the classroom. The public are ready to get behind the scheme and are keen to take advantage of the discounts available. As trusted pillars of their communities, schools play a vital role in connecting families with important information. We need you to help spread the word. So please share details of the Great British Summer Savings scheme through your newsletters, school apps, and other communications to parents and carers, so that the families in your school community know about the experiences they can enjoy this summer for less. This forms part of a broader effort by the Government to ease financial pressures on families. From ending the two-child limit and expanding free school meals, to rolling out free breakfast clubs and delivering 30 hours of free childcare, this Government is taking action to put more money back into parents' pockets and give every child the best possible start in life. As part of this campaign, we have launched an attraction finder website which allows families to type in their postcode and find participating venues near them to make the most of summer savings. To use the attraction finder, please visit https://summersavings.gov.uk. Businesses can find out more about the VAT reduction by visiting GOV.UK and searching 'Temporary reduced rate of VAT for family attractions'. Yours sincerely, RT HON BRIDGET PHILLIPSON MP Secretary of State for Education RT HON RACHEL REEVES MP Chancellor of the Exchequer

Design and Technology
Why Careers in the Curriculum?
At The Malling School, we believe that careers education is most effective when it is embedded throughout a student's learning journey rather than delivered as a series of standalone events. By helping students understand the relevance of their subjects to future education, training and employment, we encourage them to develop ambition, raise aspirations and make informed decisions about their next steps. Our aim is to equip every student with the knowledge, skills and confidence to thrive in an ever-changing world of work and to become adaptable, lifelong learners.
Careers in the Curriculum
At The Malling School, we recognise the important role that curriculum learning plays in helping students understand the relevance of their education to future careers. Our ambition is to further strengthen the links between subjects and the world of work, enabling students to recognise how the knowledge and skills they develop in lessons can support a wide range of education, training and employment pathways.
As part of this commitment, we are continuing to work with subject leaders and teaching staff to identify opportunities to embed careers learning within the curriculum. Throughout the year, Careers in the Spotlight assemblies introduce students to a range of employment sectors, employers, technical pathways, apprenticeships and higher education opportunities, broadening their awareness of future possibilities. Careers education is also delivered through our Period 1 programme, where students participate in planned activities that develop employability skills, explore labour market information and support informed decision-making at key transition points.
To support colleagues in embedding careers learning, resources, labour market information and teaching materials are shared through the school's shared drive and Unifrog. We also value regular staff feedback and collaboration, using staff voice to share effective practice, identify new opportunities and inform the ongoing development of careers education across the curriculum. As our programme continues to develop, we will work closely with curriculum areas to ensure that meaningful careers learning becomes an increasingly integral part of every student's educational experience.
Gatsby Benchmark 4, Linking curriculum learning to careers explained
What is a Gatsby Benchmark?
Gatsby Benchmarks | The Careers and Enterprise Company In our careers work we are governed by a set of standards called Gatsby Benchmarks. There are 8 of these and we work incredibly hard at The Malling School in order to meet these standards and even go above and beyond. Gatsby Benchmark 4 is a particular area in which teaching staff can help us to excel. This benchmark requires, “all teachers to link curriculum learning with careers”
Gatsby Benchmark 4, Linking Curriculum Learning to Careers
“Careers in the curriculum describes a range of interventions which allow students to encounter career learning as part of their everyday school curriculum.” You can read more about this benchmark by clicking below: Gatsby Benchmark 4 | CEC Resource Directory (careersandenterprise.co.uk)

Headteacher’s Welcome
Caring, Determined and Reflective
At The Malling School, we believe every young person deserves to be known, to belong and to be inspired to achieve their very best. We are proud to be a caring, ambitious and inclusive community where high expectations are matched by genuine kindness, and where every young person is supported to flourish academically, personally and socially while being empowered to shape their own future.
Our vision is to transform lives by providing opportunities for all pupils to achieve their maximum potential in a happy, safe and inclusive environment. Everything we do is driven by this vision, from the quality of teaching in our classrooms to the relationships we build with young people, families and the wider community.
At the heart of our school are our values of Caring, Determined and Reflective. Together they define The Malling School Way and shape a culture where every young person is known as an individual, encouraged to embrace new opportunities and supported to fulfil their potential. We also know that our staff are our greatest strength. By investing in their professional development and wellbeing, we create an environment where both adults and young people can flourish.
Learning at The Malling School is ambitious, inclusive and enriching. Through a knowledge-rich curriculum, exceptional pastoral care and a wide range of opportunities beyond the classroom, we encourage every young person to discover their strengths, develop confidence and resilience, and build the knowledge, skills and character needed for life beyond school.
While academic achievement is important, we believe education is about much more than examination results. It is about helping young people become curious, reflective and open-minded learners, confident communicators, and principled, caring individuals who think critically, embrace challenge and make informed choices about their future. Our ambition is that every young person leaves The Malling School equipped not simply to succeed in education or employment, but to shape their own future and pursue whatever success means to them.
We know the best outcomes are achieved when schools and families work together, and we value the trust that parents and carers place in us. Our commitment to inclusion, character education and high expectations has been recognised nationally through our School of Character Kitemark Plus accreditation and Inclusion Quality Mark Flagship School status, reflecting the culture we strive to create every day.
I hope this information gives you a genuine insight into our community, our values and our ambitions for every young person. I look forward to welcoming you to The Malling School.
Mrs Karen Davey, Headteacher
